title: Decree on the introduction of the West European calendar
author: The Council of People's Commissars of the Russian Republic
excerpt:
**Декрет о введении западноевропейского календаря.** 24 января (6 февраля) 1918 г.

В целях установления в России одинакового почти со всеми культурными народами исчисления времени Совет Народных Комиссаров постановляет ввести, по истечении января месяца сего года, в гражданский обиход новый календарь. В силу этого:

1) Первый день после 31 января сего года считать не 1 февраля, а 14 февраля, второй день - считать 15 и т.д.

2) Сроки всех обязательств, как по договору, так и по закону, которые наступили бы, по до сих пор действовавшему календарю, между 1 и 14 февраля, считать наступившими между 14 и 27 февраля, путем прибавления к каждому соответствующему сроку 13 дней.

[...]

10) До 1 июля с.г. писать, после числа каждого дня по новому календарю, в скобках число по до сих действовавшему календарю.

Председатель Совета Народных Комиссаров В. Ульянов (Ленин). Помощник народного комиссара по иностранным делам Чичерин. Народные комиссары: А. Шляпников. Г. Петровский. В. Алгасов. В. Оболенский. Секретарь Совета Народных Комиссаров Горбунов.
translation:
**Decree on the introduction of the West European calendar.** 24 January (6 February) 1918.

With a view to establishing in Russia a reckoning of time almost the same as that of all civilised peoples, the Council of People's Commissars resolves to introduce into civil use, at the expiry of the month of January of this year, a new calendar. In consequence:

1) The first day after 31 January of this year is to be counted not as 1 February but as 14 February; the second day as the 15th, and so on.

2) The falling due of all obligations, whether by contract or by law, which under the calendar in force until now would have fallen between 1 and 14 February, is to be counted as falling between 14 and 27 February, by the addition of 13 days to each corresponding term.

[Clauses 3 to 9 do the same arithmetic for loan interest, for salaries paid at the end of the month, on the 15th and 30th, and on the 20th, and for pensions.]

10) Until 1 July of this year, after the number of each day by the new calendar, write in brackets the number by the calendar in force until now.

Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars, V. Ulyanov (Lenin). Assistant People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs, Chicherin. People's Commissars: A. Shlyapnikov, G. Petrovsky, V. Algasov, V. Obolensky. Secretary of the Council of People's Commissars, Gorbunov.

*Translated for this pack; no scholarly English translation was available from here. Clauses 3-9 are summarised rather than translated and are marked as such - they are eight variations on the same piece of arithmetic.*
archive: Декреты Советской власти, том I (Moscow, 1957), pp. 404-405; transcribed by the electronic library of the Faculty of History, Moscow State University. The decree was agreed by the Council on 24 January (6 February) and signed on 26 January (8 February) 1918.

title: The Peace Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, Articles I to V
author: Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria and Turkey on the one part, and Russia on the other
excerpt:
**Article I.** Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria and Turkey on the one hand and Russia on the other declare that the condition of war between them has ceased.

**Article II.** The contracting parties will refrain from all agitation or propaganda against the governments or all state and military institutions of the other side.

**Article III.** The territories lying to the west of the line determined by the contracting powers and which formerly belonged to Russia will no longer be under her sovereignty.

**Article IV.** Germany is ready, as soon as general peace is established and Russian demobilization will have completely taken place, to vacate the territories lying east of the line mentioned in part 1 of Article 3.

**Article V.** Russia will, without delay, proceed to demobilize her army, including those army units newly formed by her present government.
archive: Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1918, Russia, vol. I, reproduced by the Avalon Project, Yale Law School. **This is the United States State Department's English text, not the German or Russian original**, and its article numbering is the one quoted here. The map that the treaty makes an essential part of itself, and which is what Article III actually means, is not reproduced with it - which is why this pack draws no line for the frontier the treaty created.

title: Resolution of the Council of People's Commissars on the Red Terror
author: The Council of People's Commissars
excerpt: The Council of People's Commissars, having heard the report of the Chairman of the All-Russian Extraordinary Commission for Combating Counter-revolution, Speculation and Crime about the activities of this Commission, finds: that in the present situation the safeguarding of the rear by means of terror is necessary; that it is necessary to send a greater number of responsible party comrades to the All-Russian Extraordinary Commission for Combating Counter-revolution, Speculation and Crime in order to strengthen its work and to introduce into it a more systematic character; that it is necessary to safeguard the Soviet Republic from class enemies by isolating them in concentration camps; that all persons associated with White Guard organizations, plots and rebellions are liable to be shot; that it is necessary to publish the names of all those shot and the reasons for shooting them.

title: The Petropavlovsk resolution
author: The general meeting of the crews of the battleships Petropavlovsk and Sevastopol, Kronstadt
archive: First published in Pravda o Kronshtadte (Prague, 1921); English translation from Paul Avrich (ed.), The Anarchists in the Russian Revolution (Cornell University Press, 1973), read in the Marxists Internet Archive's reproduction, which carries no pagination. **One editorial mark:** the transcription reads 'Petrograd, Constant, and Petrograd province' in clause 4; 'Constant' is plainly a corruption of Kronstadt and is corrected here in square brackets. Nothing else is altered.
